biography: Ricardo Di Loreto, born in the bustling heart of São Paulo, Brazil, didn't inherit racing; he discovered it. While his family ran a successful construction business, Ricardo found solace and adrenaline in the local karting scene. He'd sneak off after school, the roar of the tiny engines a stark contrast to the city's cacophony. His raw talent quickly became apparent, earning him a spot in a regional championship. A defining moment came at Interlagos in his early 20s, battling wheel-to-wheel with a future F1 hopeful – a race he narrowly lost but one that cemented his ambition. Now, at 37, Ricardo finds himself with Puma P052, a team struggling to stay competitive. While his steady hands and experience are valued, the shine of potential has faded, replaced by the grit of a seasoned veteran fighting for every position. He's no longer chasing championships; he's chasing the pure joy of the race, a joy that first ignited on those dusty karting tracks.
drivingStyle: Di Loreto is known for his incredibly smooth and consistent driving style. He's not one for aggressive overtakes or daring maneuvers; instead, he meticulously plans his passes and focuses on preserving his tires. Ricardo is a master of tire management, often able to extract a few extra laps from a set when others are struggling with grip. While he may lack the outright pace of some of his rivals, his consistency and ability to avoid mistakes make him a formidable opponent over the course of a race.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their karting days. Silva, known for his aggressive driving, often clashed with Di Loreto's more conservative approach, leading to several on-track incidents and heated exchanges off the track.

Rossi, a rising star, represents the new generation of drivers. Di Loreto feels she lacks respect for the older guard, while Rossi sees Di Loreto as a relic of the past, unwilling to adapt to the changing landscape of racing.
Tanaka and Di Loreto were teammates at a previous team. Their competition for the lead spot eventually devolved into sabotage and backstabbing, creating a bitter and lasting animosity.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, gifted to him by his grandmother, for every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Always circles his car three times counter-clockwise before the start of each race.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about understanding the dance between man and machine. It's about finding that perfect rhythm, that harmonious balance."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Stock Car Championship in 2015. After years of near misses, Di Loreto finally clinched the title with a dominant performance in the final race at Interlagos, fulfilling a lifelong dream in front of his home crowd.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2018. After a grueling race, Di Loreto lost control in the Porsche Curves, costing his team a likely victory and leaving him devastated.
